newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: No plan to cut Malaysia statutory reserve - minister.
newsitem.headline: No plan to cut Malaysia statutory reserve - minister.

text.p: Malaysia's Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar said on Tuesday there was no plan to cut banks' statutory reserve requirement (SRR).
He said there was sufficient liquidity in the country's banking system.
"We have good liquidity at present. If we cut the statutory reserves then we are releasing more money into the market and then you are going to affect inflation," he told reporters on Labuan island.
Asked about recent market speculation that the SRR would be reduced, he said: "The rumours are not true."
Malaysia's financial markets last week speculated that the SRR, deposits that banks keep interest-free with the central bank, would be trimmed last week from its current 13.5 percent level.
The SRR has been raised by two percentage points since the beginning of 1996.
Asked about Malaysian interest rates, Affifuddin said: "Interest rates are stable, there's not very much fluctuations".
He said the central Bank Negara retains its policy of minimum market intervention and letting market forces dictate the direction of rates.
"But if we see conditions that will bring harm to the economy, we have to intervene a bit. We can't leave it alone," he said.
Commenting on the huge deficit in the April trade figures, the minister said this was due to the "bunching up of payments" for aircraft and other big-ticket items.
Malaysia reported a 2.1 billion ringgit trade gap in April.
